angle: Myth-vs-truth quiz (A oxygen kam hona / B thand / C pressure kam, "jawab end mein") on the Leh dal puzzle: dal boils in Leh but softens slowly in an open pot. Chain: Leh about 3,500 m, so air pressure about two-thirds, so water boils at about 88 C and stays stuck there. More flame only makes more steam, so dal does soften but takes much longer. Answer C is the main cause; oxygen and cold do not set the boiling point. Fix: pressure cooker in Leh (about 115 C), a bit more time, open only when the pressure is fully out. Then the A/B/C comment prompt and the channel end card.

DESCRIPTION / PINNED COMMENT: this is a feed-curiosity video; use the Ladakh, Leh and 'pressure cooker kaise kaam karta hai' angles in tags and description. Put in the description: low oxygen matters for people and stove flames, not for the temperature of boiling water; do not tamper with the valve; let the pressure fall on its own and do not push or lift the vent weight (dal foams and can spit); never force the lid; follow the cooker manual. The fix text says fill no more than 1/3 for tuvar and moong and 1/2 for lentils; I could not verify that, so tell the creator to check his own cooker manual (many manuals say at most half for dal). No correction comment is needed now that the title says 'der se galti hai'; if he insists on 'nahi galti', pin: 'Galti hai, bas bahut der mein. Cooker use karo, aur pressure poora nikalne ke baad hi kholo.' The syringe demo stays out and is a good Part 2.
